boundary_rationale: A first-person rhetorical question returns to the prophet's own voice: עַל מִ֨י אֲדַבְּרָ֤ה וְאָעִ֨ידָה֙ וְיִשְׁמָ֔עוּ (oshb:Jer.6.10, byte tier), “To whom should I speak and testify, that they may hear?” (web:Jer.6.10). At Jer.6.11 the voice claims to be “full of Yahweh’s wrath” and “weary with holding it in” (web:Jer.6.11), then turns to the imperative שְׁפֹ֤ךְ (oshb:Jer.6.11, byte tier); whether the surrounding voice is the prophet describing his own experience of carrying the divine wrath, or Yahweh's own voice continuing, is not settled by any explicit marker, so the verse is held with the surrounding material rather than cut. Jer.6.12 closes on the postpositive formula נְאֻם יְהוָֽה (oshb:Jer.6.12, byte tier), and Jer.6.15 closes on אָמַ֥ר יְהוָֽה (oshb:Jer.6.15, byte tier); both are closure corroboration (non-driving), since no fresh tier-1 onset opens at Jer.6.13, which begins on a bare causal particle, כִּ֤י (oshb:Jer.6.13, byte tier), governing the universal-corruption indictment, “from their least even to their greatest” (web:Jer.6.13). The unit continues through the false “Peace, peace” (web:Jer.6.14) of those who claim there is peace “when there is no peace” (web:Jer.6.14), and the shameless refusal to blush at Jer.6.15.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Reject splitting the universal-corruption indictment (Jer.6.13-Jer.6.15) from the wrath-bearing verses: Jer.6.13 opens on the bare causal particle כִּ֤י with no imperative, vocative, or formula of its own, so nothing at that verse argues an independent onset.
literature_type_guess: prophet's wrath-bearing indictment of universal corruption
wj_or_red_letter_considered: not applicable in the OT substrate
device_notes: The WLC paragraph-mark layer records a setumah at Jer.6.15 (single-witness; Prophets tier-3, carrying no boundary weight here), on this unit's own closing verse. The seg inventory records 2 paseq segs in this span, at MT 6:11 and MT 6:14 (single-witness; count-only, no intra-verse position sourced). Frontier flag: whether Jer.6.11's claim to be full of Yahweh's wrath voices the prophet's own experience or Yahweh's continuing speech is held open; the unit does not resolve it.

boundary_rationale: A koh-amar formula restarts the frame: כֹּ֣ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֡ה עִמְדוּ֩ עַל דְּרָכִ֨ים (oshb:Jer.6.16, byte tier), “Stand in the ways and see, and ask for the old paths” (web:Jer.6.16), answered by the people's refusal, וַיֹּאמְר֖וּ לֹ֥א נֵלֵֽךְ (oshb:Jer.6.16, byte tier), “We will not walk in it” (web:Jer.6.16). The same command-and-refusal shape reproduces itself inside the reported watchmen speech of Jer.6.17: הַקְשִׁ֖יבוּ לְק֣וֹל שׁוֹפָ֑ר (oshb:Jer.6.17, byte tier), “Listen to the sound of the trumpet!” (web:Jer.6.17), answered in the same verse by וַיֹּאמְר֖וּ לֹ֥א נַקְשִֽׁיב (oshb:Jer.6.17, byte tier), “We will not listen!” (web:Jer.6.17); no fresh koh-amar restart separates Jer.6.17 from the formula that opens Jer.6.16, before the nations-summons imperative at Jer.6.18 addresses a new audience.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Reject folding the witness-summons (Jer.6.18) into this row: its imperative addresses a new audience (the nations, as witnesses) distinct from the "they said" refusal reported of Judah in Jer.6.16-Jer.6.17.
wj_or_red_letter_considered: not applicable in the OT substrate
device_notes: A setumah stands at Jer.6.15 in the Masoretic paragraph layer (single-witness disclosure; tier-3 weak corroboration (non-driving)) as this unit's front seam. The seg inventory records 1 paseq at MT 6:16, inside this span (single-witness; count-only, no intra-verse position sourced).

boundary_rationale: A fresh imperative addresses a new audience, though the particle opening it points backward: לָכֵ֖ן שִׁמְע֣וּ הַגּוֹיִ֑ם (oshb:Jer.6.18, byte tier), “Therefore hear, you nations” (web:Jer.6.18) - the consequence connective לָכֵ֖ן binds this summons to the refusal reported at Jer.6.16-Jer.6.17, yet no formula overrides it as one does at Jer.6.21, so the imperative-plus-vocative shape still carries the onset. The summons is echoed at שִׁמְעִ֣י הָאָ֔רֶץ (oshb:Jer.6.19, byte tier), “Hear, earth!” (web:Jer.6.19) - the nations and the earth are summoned as witnesses, distinct from the direct address to Judah in Jer.6.16-Jer.6.17. The witness-summons runs through the rejected-offerings question at Jer.6.20, “your sacrifices are not pleasing to me” (web:Jer.6.20), without a further imperative or vocative marking a fresh onset.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Reject splitting the rejected-offerings question (Jer.6.20) from the witness summons: it carries no vocative, imperative, or second-person verb of its own, unlike the vocative-bearing imperatives at שִׁמְע֣וּ הַגּוֹיִ֑ם (oshb:Jer.6.18, byte tier) and שִׁמְעִ֣י הָאָ֔רֶץ (oshb:Jer.6.19, byte tier), and its plural possessors, עֹלֽוֹתֵיכֶם֙ and וְזִבְחֵיכֶ֖ם (oshb:Jer.6.20, byte tier), resume the same second-person-plural addressee already reached at לְנַפְשְׁכֶ֑ם (oshb:Jer.6.16, byte tier) and עֲלֵיכֶם֙ (oshb:Jer.6.17, byte tier) rather than opening a fresh one.
wj_or_red_letter_considered: not applicable in the OT substrate
device_notes: WLC marks Jer.6.20, this unit's own closing verse, with a setumah (single-witness; tier-3 in the Prophets, not used to justify this cut). The second-person-plural possessors at Jer.6.20, עֹלֽוֹתֵיכֶם֙ and וְזִבְחֵיכֶ֖ם (oshb:Jer.6.20, byte tier), address the people rather than the nations and the earth summoned as witnesses at Jer.6.18-Jer.6.19.

boundary_rationale: A fresh grammatical subject opens this unit: שָׁמַ֥עְנוּ אֶת שָׁמְע֖וֹ רָפ֣וּ יָדֵ֑ינוּ (oshb:Jer.6.24, byte tier), “We have heard its report. Our hands become feeble” (web:Jer.6.24) - a first-person-plural communal voice replacing the third-person description of the invading army at Jer.6.22-Jer.6.23. Jer.6.25 turns to a second-person prohibition addressed to that same community (a verse carrying two ketiv/qere notes, a doubled-note verse, quoted here at the qere): אַל תצאי תֵּֽצְאוּ֙ הַשָּׂדֶ֔ה ... אַל תלכי תֵּלֵ֑כוּ (oshb:Jer.6.25, byte tier), “Don’t go out into the field or walk by the way” (web:Jer.6.25), before the vocative-marked mourning summons to the daughter of my people at Jer.6.26.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Reject extending this unit through the mourning summons (Jer.6.26): the vocative "daughter of my people" opens a fresh direct address not present in the first-person-plural voice of Jer.6.24 or the second-person prohibition of Jer.6.25.
wj_or_red_letter_considered: not applicable in the OT substrate
device_notes: The two ketiv/qere notes at Jer.6.25 (a doubled-note verse) vary the addressee's person and number: the unpointed ketiv forms, תצאי and תלכי (oshb:Jer.6.25, source bytes), are second-person feminine singular, while the pointed qere forms the citation reads, תֵּֽצְאוּ֙ and תֵּלֵ֑כוּ (oshb:Jer.6.25, byte tier), are second-person masculine plural. Under the written form, this verse's address class continues into חִגְרִי and עֲשִׂ֣י לָ֔ךְ (oshb:Jer.6.26, byte tier) at Jer.6.26 across the back seam, and matches the class already closing Jer.6.23 at עָלַ֖יִךְ (oshb:Jer.6.23, byte tier) across the front seam.

boundary_rationale: A vocative-plus-imperative mourning summons opens and carries this unit's own cut: בַּת עַמִּ֤י חִגְרִי שָׂק֙ (oshb:Jer.6.26, byte tier), “Daughter of my people, clothe yourself with sackcloth” (web:Jer.6.26), continuing “and wallow in ashes!” (web:Jer.6.26) - direct address to the personified community by name, a marker neither Jer.6.24 nor Jer.6.25 carries. The unit's own closing suffix, עָלֵֽינוּ (oshb:Jer.6.26, byte tier), “for the destroyer will suddenly come on us” (web:Jer.6.26), continues the first-person-plural voice that opened at Jer.6.24 across this unit's own front seam; the tie is disclosed rather than argued against the cut, since the vocative-plus-imperative onset carries it independently.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Reject folding this verse into the material that precedes it: its vocative "daughter of my people" and imperative "clothe yourself" distinctly address a personified addressee, matching the same marker class used at Jer.4.14 and Jer.6.1, a marker neither the first-person-plural voice of Jer.6.24 nor the second-person prohibition of Jer.6.25 carries.
literature_type_guess: mourning summons to daughter of my people
